cards.title: Cards for your Home Assistant dashboard
cards.intro: Two separate installs from the Marketplace that draw what is in Home Assistant: screen time against a limit, and the night as a hypnogram. Open source and free.

android.name: Android app
android.line: Health Connect and screen time per app
android.req_short: Android 8.0 or newer; health data from Android 9.
android.requires: Android 9 or newer with Health Connect for health data; Android 8.0 or newer for screen time.
android.free_line: Other ways to install the same app, with the same signing key:

play.name: Google Play
play.pitch: €4.99 once on Google Play: the easy way, with automatic updates, and it supports development.
play.note: €4.99 once (US$4.99), no subscription. The easy way: Google Play installs it and keeps it up to date, and buying it supports development. It's listed there as Health Data for Home Assistant.
play.soon_text: Google Play: coming, as a paid listing of the same app

apk.name: APK on GitHub
apk.note: Open it on your phone and allow installs from your browser once. Each new release is on GitHub, or Obtainium updates it for you.

obtainium.name: Obtainium
obtainium.note: An app updater for GitHub apps: installs the same APK and keeps it up to date. Open this link on your phone.

fdroid.name: F-Droid
fdroid.note: Built by F-Droid from the source and identical to the signed APK; the F-Droid app keeps it up to date.
fdroid.soon_text: F-Droid: accepted, the listing goes live with its next build

ios.name: iPhone app
ios.line: Apple Health, with the same payload
ios.req_short: iOS 17 or newer. On the App Store, or build it yourself on a Mac.
ios.requires: iOS 17 or newer. Building it yourself needs a Mac with Xcode and an Apple Developer Program membership, because a free Apple Account can't sign an app that reads Apple Health.

appstore.name: App Store
appstore.pitch: €6.99 once on the App Store, no subscription.
appstore.note: €6.99 once (US$5.99), no subscription. No Mac needed, and it updates like any other app.

xcode.name: Build with Xcode
xcode.note: From source, on a Mac with Xcode and an Apple Developer Program membership: about an hour the first time. Your settings stay when you run a newer version.

home-assistant.name: Home Assistant integration
home-assistant.full: Life Dashboard integration for Home Assistant
home-assistant.line: Sensors, statistics and all your history
home-assistant.requires: Home Assistant 2026.3 or newer. HACS only on versions before 2026.11.

hacs.name: HACS
hacs.note: In Settings > Marketplace (HACS before Home Assistant 2026.11), search for Life Dashboard. On HACS, restart Home Assistant after the download.

ha-setup.name: Setup steps
ha-setup.note: Add the integration, check the address the phone should use, scan the QR code.

ha-source.name: Source on GitHub
ha-source.note: Release notes and the manual install.

grafana.name: Grafana stack
grafana.line: Postgres, Grafana, an API and MCP, self-hosted
grafana.requires: Docker with Compose on a machine your phone can reach, or a Kubernetes cluster with Helm.

compose.name: Docker Compose
compose.note: Download docker-compose.yml and the example .env from the latest release, set the secret, your time zone, the address and the passwords, then docker compose up -d. Nothing to clone or build.

demo.name: Demo data
demo.note: 60 days of made-up data for two phones, from the same compose file, before any phone of yours is involved.

helm.name: Helm chart for Kubernetes
helm.note: The same images on a cluster of your own, with Postgres from CloudNativePG, a bundled StatefulSet or a database you already run.

screen-time-card.name: Screen time cards
screen-time-card.line: Today, the week and the family, against a daily limit
screen-time-card.req_short: Three cards in one install. Home Assistant 2026.3 or newer.
screen-time-card.requires: Home Assistant 2026.3 or newer. HACS only on versions before 2026.11.

hacs.name: HACS
hacs.note: In Settings > Marketplace (HACS before Home Assistant 2026.11), search for Life Dashboard Screen Time and download it. All three cards are then in the card picker.

card-guide.name: Screen time guide
card-guide.note: Screen time per app from an Android phone into Home Assistant, step by step.

ha-source.name: Source on GitHub
ha-source.note: Release notes, every option and the install by hand.

sleep-card.name: Sleep card
sleep-card.line: One night of sleep as a hypnogram
sleep-card.req_short: For Android and iPhone. Home Assistant 2026.3 or newer.
sleep-card.requires: Home Assistant 2026.3 or newer. HACS only on versions before 2026.11.

hacs.name: HACS
hacs.note: In Settings > Marketplace (HACS before Home Assistant 2026.11), search for Life Dashboard Sleep Card and download it. Then add it from the card picker.

card-guide.name: Sleep stages guide
card-guide.note: The sensors and statistics per night, and the card on a dashboard, step by step.

ha-source.name: Source on GitHub
ha-source.note: Release notes, every option and the install by hand.

status.android: It's on Google Play for €4.99 once (US$4.99), no subscription: the easy way, with automatic updates, and buying it supports development. The free routes install the same app with the same signing key: the signed APK from GitHub, Obtainium, which keeps that APK up to date, and F-Droid, which builds it from the source.

health-connect-home-assistant.name: Health Connect in Home Assistant
health-connect-home-assistant.desc: Samsung Health, Garmin, Fitbit, Oura and Withings data as sensors, with all your history.
health-connect-home-assistant.next: Two installs: the integration from the Marketplace or HACS and the app on your phone. After that, pairing takes a minute.

samsung-health-home-assistant.name: Samsung Health and Galaxy Watch in Home Assistant
samsung-health-home-assistant.desc: Steps, sleep, heart rate and workouts through Health Connect, with no Samsung login.
samsung-health-home-assistant.next: Two installs: the integration from the Marketplace or HACS and the app on your phone. After that, switch on Health Connect in Samsung Health and pair with one QR code.

companion-app-health-connect.name: The companion app and Health Connect
companion-app-health-connect.desc: When its 36 sensors are enough, and what history, backfill and 34 types add.
companion-app-health-connect.next: Keep the companion app. Add the integration from the Marketplace or HACS and the app on your phone, pair with one QR code, then run a backfill.

health-connect-webhook.name: Health Connect to a webhook
health-connect-webhook.desc: The JSON payload, signatures, retries and receivers for n8n and Node-RED.
health-connect-webhook.next: Install the app, point it at your URL and tap Send test. The payload reference has every field and a receiver in Python and Node.js.

screen-time-home-assistant.name: Screen time in Home Assistant
screen-time-home-assistant.desc: Minutes per app as sensors, limits you set yourself, and several phones.
screen-time-home-assistant.next: Screen time doesn't need Health Connect. Any phone or tablet with Android 8.0 or newer works.
buttons: Open the integration in the Marketplace

sleep-stages-home-assistant.name: Sleep stages in Home Assistant
sleep-stages-home-assistant.desc: Deep, light, REM and awake per night as sensors and statistics, and a card that draws the night.
sleep-stages-home-assistant.next: The card is one install from the Marketplace. The night it draws comes from the integration and the app on your phone, or on Android from the Companion app's Sleep duration sensor.
buttons: Open the card in the Marketplace

smart-scale-to-samsung-health.name: Smart scale to Samsung Health
smart-scale-to-samsung-health.desc: Weight, body fat and blood pressure from Home Assistant into Health Connect.
smart-scale-to-samsung-health.next: You need the Life Dashboard integration 0.7.0 or newer and the app on your phone, paired as in the Health Connect guide.

health-connect-n8n.name: Health Connect to n8n
health-connect-n8n.desc: A Webhook node, an HMAC check in a Code node, then Postgres, Sheets or Telegram.
health-connect-n8n.next: Install the app, put the production URL of your published workflow in it and tap Send test. The payload reference has the same check with a Crypto node.

health-connect-data-types.name: Health Connect data types, app by app
health-connect-data-types.desc: All 34 types with keys and units, and what Samsung, Garmin, Fitbit and Oura write.
health-connect-data-types.next: Pick your types under What to send on the Health tab and tap Preview payload to see what the next sync would send.

health-data-api.name: A web API for Health Connect or Apple Health
health-data-api.desc: Why neither has one, and how to get the data onto your server anyway.
health-data-api.next: Install the app on the phone and point it at your URL. The payload reference has every field and a receiver in Python and Node.js.

samsung-health-export.name: Samsung Health to your own server
samsung-health-export.desc: Galaxy Watch data as JSON in your own database, n8n flow or script.
samsung-health-export.next: Switch on Health Connect in Samsung Health, install the app, and tap Send test against your URL.

fitbit-home-assistant.name: Fitbit and Pixel Watch in Home Assistant
fitbit-home-assistant.desc: Through Health Connect, with no Fitbit Web API and no Google Cloud project.
fitbit-home-assistant.next: Two installs: the integration from the Marketplace or HACS and the app on your phone. After that, pairing takes a minute.

garmin-home-assistant.name: Garmin in Home Assistant
garmin-home-assistant.desc: Steps, sleep and heart rate from Garmin Connect, with no Garmin login in Home Assistant.
garmin-home-assistant.next: Two installs: the integration from the Marketplace or HACS and the app on your phone. After that, switch on Health Connect in Garmin Connect and pair with one QR code.

health-data-own-ai.name: Health Connect and Apple Health over MCP
health-data-own-ai.desc: The stack's read-only MCP server lets a local model or Claude read your history. Works in Europe too.
health-data-own-ai.next: Start with the data: the stack or the integration, and a backfill of all your history from the app.

health-data-qr-pairing.name: Let your users connect with one QR code
health-data-qr-pairing.desc: For your own service: the pairing link, a generator in Python and Node.js, and the signed test ping.
health-data-qr-pairing.next: Build a code for one test user and scan it with the app. The pairing reference has every rule, the test vector and the iPhone differences.

health-connect-steps-home-assistant.name: Health Connect steps that look wrong in Home Assistant
health-connect-steps-home-assistant.desc: Sensors that lag, steps after midnight, totals that go down, and day totals that are replaced per day.
health-connect-steps-home-assistant.next: Compare the total in Health Connect with Home Assistant first. For day totals that are replaced per day, install the integration and pair the app with its QR code.

troubleshooting.name: Troubleshooting: syncs, sensors and pairing
troubleshooting.desc: Syncs that stop in the background, Health Connect permissions, missing sensors and pairing, step by step.
troubleshooting.next: Still stuck? Ask in Discussions and include the row from the Logs tab; the setup guide has the full list of known problems.

apple-health-home-assistant.name: Apple Health in Home Assistant
apple-health-home-assistant.desc: Apple Watch and iPhone data as sensors, with all your history from a backfill.
apple-health-home-assistant.next: Two installs: the integration from the Marketplace or HACS and the app on your iPhone. After that, pair with one QR code and run a backfill.

apple-health-home-assistant-apps.name: Apple Health in Home Assistant: four apps compared
apple-health-home-assistant-apps.desc: The companion app, HealthSync, Health Assistant Link and Life Dashboard side by side: price, history and what arrives.
apple-health-home-assistant-apps.next: For Life Dashboard: the integration from the Marketplace or HACS and the app on your iPhone, paired with one QR code. The setup guide has every step.

apple-watch-home-assistant.name: Apple Watch in Home Assistant
apple-watch-home-assistant.desc: Heart rate, HRV, sleep stages, workouts and VO2 max from the watch, through Apple Health.
apple-watch-home-assistant.next: Your watch already writes to Apple Health. Add the integration from the Marketplace or HACS and the app on your iPhone, and pair with one QR code.

apple-health-webhook.name: Apple Health to a webhook
apple-health-webhook.desc: Signed JSON from Apple Health, automatically: the payload, retries, deletions and Shortcuts.
apple-health-webhook.next: Install the app, add your URL and tap Test ping. The iOS payload page lists everything an iPhone sends.

apple-health-n8n.name: Apple Health to n8n
apple-health-n8n.desc: The same Webhook node and HMAC check as for Android, and what differs in an iPhone payload.
apple-health-n8n.next: Install the app, put the production URL of your published workflow in it and tap Test ping. The payload reference has the same check with a Crypto node.

apple-health-data-types.name: Apple Health data types, app by app
apple-health-data-types.desc: All 28 types the iPhone app reads, with payload keys, units and what writes them.
apple-health-data-types.next: Switch on your types under What to send and tap Preview payload to see what the next sync would send.

android.description: Life Dashboard for Android is an open-source app that sends Health Connect data and screen time per app to Home Assistant, MQTT or your own webhook, with no cloud and no account.
android.operatingSystem: Android 8.0 or newer (health data: Android 9 or newer with Health Connect)
featureList: Home Assistant integration with QR pairing and all your history
Webhooks with JSON, HMAC-SHA256 signatures and client certificates
Writes scale and blood pressure readings from Home Assistant into Health Connect

ios.description: Life Dashboard for iPhone is an open-source iPhone app that sends Apple Health data to Home Assistant, MQTT or your own webhook, with no cloud and no account.

home-assistant.description: The Life Dashboard integration is an open-source Home Assistant custom integration, installed through the Marketplace or HACS, that turns data from the Life Dashboard apps into sensors and long-term statistics, paired by QR code.

grafana.description: The Life Dashboard stack is an open-source, self-hosted backend for the Life Dashboard apps: a receiver, Postgres and six Grafana dashboards, with a read-only API and an optional MCP server, installed with Docker Compose or a Helm chart.
grafana.operatingSystem: Linux, macOS or Windows with Docker, or Kubernetes
featureList: Published images for amd64 and arm64, installed with one docker-compose.yml
An MCP server with eight read-only tools
A Helm chart for Kubernetes with CloudNativePG

sleep-card.description: The Life Dashboard Sleep Card is an open-source Home Assistant dashboard card that draws one night of sleep as a hypnogram, from the Life Dashboard integration 1.1.0 or newer or, on Android, the official Home Assistant Companion app 2026.11.1 or newer.

screen-time-card.description: Life Dashboard Screen Time is an open-source set of three Home Assistant dashboard cards that show screen time for today, the week and the whole family against a daily limit, from the Life Dashboard integration, Google Family Link, Microsoft Family Safety or any sensor with today's total.
featureList: Today on one phone against a daily limit
The week as a bar per day
The whole family in one card
A built-in list of 126 Android apps with their color and icon
Reads Google Family Link and Microsoft Family Safety

project_description: Open-source project by Owen Vogelaar: apps for Android and iPhone that send health data to Home Assistant, MQTT or a webhook, a Home Assistant integration and a self-hosted Grafana stack.

projects.Health Assistant: A self-hosted health record. Its webhook integration has a parser for the Life Dashboard payload and calls the app “Highly Recommended for Android Users”.
projects.HealthQuery: A personal health dashboard in SQLite, with reports and an MCP server. Its data comes from the Life Dashboard app.
projects.fitbridge: Health Connect for ChatGPT and Claude, self-hosted on Cloudflare Workers. The app pairs with it by QR code and sends it signed updates.
